definitions.gloss: unchanged; as always; as before; without change
definitions.explanation: Remaining the same as before; continuing in the same state without alteration. Often used to express that something persists over time.

examples.japanese: {相変|あいか}わらず{元気|げんき}だね。
examples.notes: The compound {相変|あいか}わらず is the most common form in everyday speech.

examples.japanese: {十年|じゅうねん}{経|た}っても、あの{町|まち}は{変|か}わらず{静|しず}かだ。
examples.english: Even after ten years, that town is quiet, just as it was before.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}と{変|か}わらず、{毎朝|まいあさ}ジョギングを{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: Just as in the past, I continue jogging every morning.

notes:
{変|か}わらず is the negative continuative form (ず form) of {変|か}わる (to change), functioning as an adverb meaning "without changing." It expresses constancy or persistence of a state.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {相変|あいか}わらず: as always; as usual — the most frequently used form, often with a nuance of mild exasperation or familiarity
- {昔|むかし}と{変|か}わらず: same as in the old days
- {今|いま}も{変|か}わらず: still the same now

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {変|か}わらず{元気|げんき}: as healthy as always
- {変|か}わらぬ{友情|ゆうじょう}: unchanging friendship
- {変|か}わらない{笑顔|えがお}: an unchanging smile

COMMON PATTERNS:
The ず form is a classical negative form that survives in modern Japanese as an adverbial. The attributive form is {変|か}わらぬ (literary) or {変|か}わらない (modern): {変|か}わらぬ{愛|あい} (unchanging love).
